title: Desk Guidance: Unrepaid Property-Charge Advances and the Successor Runway in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Rule.** For a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case on a Cedarline Summit loan reclassified on the death of the last surviving borrower, the unrepaid property-charge advances are the advances recorded on the loan's property charge repayment arrangement, less the repayments recorded on it. That arrangement is the Property Charge Advance Repayment record.

- Where the unrepaid property-charge advances exceed 2000.00 dollars and the loan's Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve is not active, 10 calendar days are taken off the runway length.
- Where they are more than zero and no more than 2000.00 dollars and that reserve is not active, 5 calendar days are taken off.
- Where there are none, or that reserve is active, nothing is taken off.

Whether the reserve is active is read from the status of the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve held for that Summit loan among the borrower's Set-Aside Accounts. A reserve with any status other than active, or no such reserve at all, is not active.

## Combinations

| Unrepaid advances | Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | Days taken off the runway length |
|---|---|---|
| more than 2000.00 dollars | not active | 10 |
| more than zero, up to and including 2000.00 dollars | not active | 5 |
| none | not active | 0 |
| any amount | active | 0 |

## Both sides of the threshold (hypothetical)

- Advances 3,100.00 less repayments 1,100.00 leaves exactly 2000.00 dollars unrepaid. That is not above the threshold, so with the reserve not active, 5 days are taken off.
- Advances 3,100.00 less repayments 1,099.99 leaves 2,000.01 dollars. With the reserve not active, 10 days are taken off.
- Advances fully repaid leaves nothing unrepaid, so nothing is taken off whatever the reserve's status.
